title: doFuture: An Overview on using Foreach to Parallelize via the Future Framework
text: doFuture package provides two alternatives using futures foreach: y <- foreach(...) %dofuture% { ... } registerDoFuture() + y <- foreach(...) %dopar% { ... }.

title: doFuture: An Overview on using Foreach to Parallelize via the Future Framework
text: first alternative (recommended), uses %dofuture%, avoids use registerDoFuture(). %dofuture% operator provides consistent behavior %dopar%, e.g. unique set foreach arguments instead one per possible adapter. Identification globals, random number generation (RNG), error handling handled future ecosystem, just like map-reduce solutions future.apply furrr. example : alternative recommended way let foreach() parallelize via future framework, especially start scratch. See help("%dofuture%", package = "doFuture") details examples approach.
code: library(doFuture) plan(multisession)  y <- foreach(x = 1:4, y = 1:10) %dofuture% {   z <- x + y   slow_sqrt(z) }

title: doFuture: An Overview on using Foreach to Parallelize via the Future Framework
text: second alternative based traditional foreach approach one registers foreach adapter used %dopar%. popular adapter doParallel::registerDoParallel(), parallelizes local machine using parallel package. package provides registerDoFuture(), parallelizes using future package, meaning future-compliant parallel backend can used. example : alternative useful already lot R code uses %dopar% just want switch using future framework parallelization. Using registerDoFuture() also useful wish use future framework packages functions uses foreach() %dopar% internally, e.g. caret, plyr, NMF, glmnet. can also used configure Bioconductor BiocParallel package, package rely , parallelize via future framework. See help("registerDoFuture", package = "doFuture") details examples approach.
code: library(doFuture) registerDoFuture() plan(multisession)  y <- foreach(x = 1:4, y = 1:10) %dopar% {   z <- x + y   slow_sqrt(z) }

title: Foreach Iteration using Futures via %dopar%

what: doFuture takes care of exports and packages automatically
title: Foreach Iteration using Futures via %dopar%
text: foreach package support automated handling globals unfortunately work cases. Specifically, foreach() called within function, need export globals explicitly. example, although global cutoff properly exported falls short soon try within function: solution explicitly export global variables, e.g. contrast, using %dopar% adapter doFuture, future machinery comes play including automatic handling global variables, e.g. indeed work. Another advantage doFuture , contrary doParallel, packages need attached also automatically taken care , e.g. whereas said , order write foreach code works everywhere, better conservative assume end users use doFuture backend. , still recommended explicitly specify objects need export whenever using foreach API. doFuture framework can help identify go .export argument. setting options(doFuture.foreach.export = ".export--automatic--warning"), doFuture warn finds globals listed .export produce informative warning message suggesting added. assert argument .export correct, test code options(doFuture.foreach.export = ".export"), disable automatic identification globals globals specified .export argument used.
code: library("doParallel") registerDoParallel(parallel::makeCluster(2))  cutoff <- 0.10 y <- foreach(x = mtcars) %dopar% {   mean(x, trim = cutoff) } names(y) <- colnames(mtcars) my_mean <- function() {   y <- foreach(x = mtcars) %dopar% {     mean(x, trim = cutoff)   }   names(y) <- colnames(mtcars)   y }  x <- my_mean() ## Error in { : task 1 failed - "object 'cutoff' not found" my_mean <- function() {   y <- foreach(x = mtcars, .export = "cutoff") %dopar% {     mean(x, trim = cutoff)   }   names(y) <- colnames(mtcars)   y }  y <- my_mean() library("doFuture") registerDoFuture() plan(multisession, workers = 2)  my_mean <- function() {   y <- foreach(x = mtcars) %dopar% {     mean(x, trim = cutoff)   }   names(y) <- colnames(mtcars)   y }  x <- my_mean() registerDoFuture() library("tools") ext <- foreach(file = c("abc.txt", "def.log")) %dopar% file_ext(file) unlist(ext) ## [1] "txt" "log" registerDoParallel(parallel::makeCluster(2)) library("tools") ext <- foreach(file = c("abc.txt", "def.log")) %dopar% file_ext(file) ## Error in file_ext(file) :  ##   task 1 failed - "could not find function "file_ext""

title: Foreach Iteration using Futures via %dopar%
text: Due generic nature futures, doFuture package provides functionality many existing doNnn packages combined, e.g. doMC, doParallel, doMPI, doSNOW.
code: library("foreach") registerDoSEQ() library("doFuture") registerDoFuture() plan(sequential) library("doMC") registerDoMC() library("doFuture") registerDoFuture() plan(multicore) library("doParallel") registerDoParallel() library("doFuture") registerDoFuture() plan(multisession)  ## on MS Windows plan(multicore)     ## on Linux, Solaris, and macOS library("doFuture") registerDoFuture() plan(future.callr::callr) library("doParallel") cl <- makeCluster(4) registerDoParallel(cl) library("doFuture") registerDoFuture() cl <- makeCluster(4) plan(cluster, workers = cl) library("doMPI") cl <- startMPIcluster(count = 4) registerDoMPI(cl) library("doFuture") registerDoFuture() cl <- makeCluster(4, type = "MPI") plan(cluster, workers = cl) library("doSNOW") cl <- makeCluster(4) registerDoSNOW(cl) library("doFuture") registerDoFuture() cl <- makeCluster(4) plan(cluster, workers = cl) library("doFuture") registerDoFuture() plan(future.batchtools::batchtools_sge) library("doRedis") registerDoRedis("jobs") startLocalWorkers(n = 4, queue = "jobs")

code: # \donttest{ library(iterators)  # iter() registerDoFuture()  # (a) tell %dopar% to use the future framework plan(multisession)  # (b) parallelize futures on the local machine   ## Example 1 A <- matrix(rnorm(100^2), nrow = 100) B <- t(A)  y1 <- apply(B, MARGIN = 2L, FUN = function(b) {   A %*% b })  y2 <- foreach(b = iter(B, by = "col"), .combine = cbind) %dopar% {   A %*% b } stopifnot(all.equal(y2, y1))    ## Example 2 - Chunking (4 elements per future [= worker]) y3 <- foreach(b = iter(B, by = "col"), .combine = cbind,               .options.future = list(chunk.size = 10)) %dopar% {   A %*% b } stopifnot(all.equal(y3, y1))   ## Example 3 - Simulation with parallel RNG library(doRNG) #> Loading required package: rngtools  my_stat <- function(x) {   median(x) }  my_experiment <- function(n, mu = 0.0, sigma = 1.0) {   ## Important: use %dorng% whenever random numbers   ##            are involved in parallel evaluation   foreach(i = 1:n) %dorng% {     x <- rnorm(i, mean = mu, sd = sigma)     list(mu = mean(x), sigma = sd(x), own = my_stat(x))   } }  ## Reproducible results when using the same RNG seed set.seed(0xBEEF) y1 <- my_experiment(n = 3)  set.seed(0xBEEF) y2 <- my_experiment(n = 3)  stopifnot(identical(y2, y1))  ## But only then y3 <- my_experiment(n = 3) str(y3) #> List of 3 #>  $ :List of 3 #>   ..$ mu   : num 1.26 #>   ..$ sigma: num NA #>   ..$ own  : num 1.26 #>  $ :List of 3 #>   ..$ mu   : num 1.33 #>   ..$ sigma: num 1.58 #>   ..$ own  : num 1.33 #>  $ :List of 3 #>   ..$ mu   : num -0.247 #>   ..$ sigma: num 1.99 #>   ..$ own  : num -0.993 #>  - attr(*, "rng")=List of 3 #>   ..$ : int [1:7] 10407 -557965149 646670728 1535601129 -1782995818 -140875233 -2010542636 #>   ..$ : int [1:7] 10407 1322665455 228081586 690246064 292190646 -1209002294 -964069472 #>   ..$ : int [1:7] 10407 1930909627 1980809480 -419043334 1761816562 811800279 -442022187 #>  - attr(*, "doRNG_version")= chr "1.7.4" stopifnot(!identical(y3, y1))  # }
